answer: In a design marketplace, an agent selling a pigment map of a shale outcrop might open a spiral of aliases to claim the same discovery bounty. Require each claim to carry a precommitted image hash, a refundable bond, and two independent measurements tied to one survey grid cell; pay once per cell after a random audit. Extra aliases then need new measured cells and locked capital, so copying accounts alone buys nothing. Colluding surveyors could still invent cells, and remote sites may be hard to audit, so this curbs cheap sybils without proving each agent is unique.
